js-array-chunk-reversal: Process the array in slices of `chunkSize`, reversing each slice; the last chunk may be shorter but still gets reversed.
js-deep-clone: Recurse into arrays and plain objects, and keep a `WeakMap` from originals to copies so circular references don't loop forever.
js-deep-equal: Compare primitives with `===`, then for objects check key counts match and recurse on each key; arrays must also match in length and order.
js-deep-find: Split the path on `.` and walk one key at a time, returning `undefined` as soon as a step hits null or undefined.
js-deep-freeze: Freeze the object, then recurse into every property value that is an object (arrays included) and freeze those too.
js-divisor-finder: Work with the absolute value of `n` and collect every number from 1 to n-1 that leaves remainder 0; 1 has no proper divisors.
js-election-mix: Return a function that loops over `Object.entries`, keeps pairs passing `criteria`, maps their values, and also counts what was kept.
js-even-sum: Add up the even numbers from 0 to `n` (step by 2, or use the arithmetic-series formula).
js-exam-grader: Race the sequential `await` of the exercises against a timeout promise with `Promise.race`, and compute the grade only if they finish first.
js-factorial: Multiply 1 through `n`, and remember that 0! is 1.
js-fibonacci: Keep the last two values and roll them forward `n` times; fibonacci(0) is 0.
js-final-attempt: Return an async function that `await`s the callback in a try/catch loop, retrying up to `count` times before throwing the last error.
js-flat-object: Recurse into plain objects with a dotted key prefix; arrays are leaves, and each of their items goes through the mapper.
js-flatten-object: Recurse with a growing dot-separated prefix; arrays are objects too, so their indices become part of the key path.
js-grid-word-finder: Build every row string and every column string, then keep the words that appear inside any of them with `includes`.
js-grid-word-finder2: No loops allowed, so use `map`, `flatMap` and `filter` over rows and columns, checking each start cell horizontally and vertically.
js-insertion-sort-analyzer: Copy the array, then for each element shift it left while the comparator says it's out of order, counting each comparison and each swap.
js-nested-array-reverser: Reverse the outer array and each inner array (on copies), flatten, and join with a single space; an empty input gives an empty string.
js-object-lab: Merge objects one by one, checking `key in result` to count added versus overwritten keys, then apply the transforms in order with `reduce`.
js-palindromic-chains: Reverse digits via string conversion, add, and re-check up to 100 times; return 0 for numbers that never become palindromes.
js-perfect-num: Sum the proper divisors (1 up to n/2) and compare to `n`; numbers below 2 are never perfect.
js-pipeline: Use `reduce` (or a loop) to pass the value through each function, recording index, input and output for every step.
js-sentence-pyramid: Split the sentence into words and log `slice(0, i).join(" ")` for growing `i`.
js-sleep-breaker: Combine a `setTimeout` promise and the `breaker()` promise with `Promise.race`, and clear the timer when the breaker wins.
js-snakepath-validator: Without loops, count the 1s and flood-fill from one of them recursively; it is valid if the fill reaches every 1.
js-swappable-object: A `Proxy` with a `get` trap can look up the key first and, failing that, find the key whose value equals the requested property.
js-transform-keys: Rebuild the object from `Object.entries`, transforming each key and recursing only when the value is a plain object.
js-trap-object: Wrap the object in a `Proxy` whose `get` and `set` traps call `fn` with the right arguments before using `Reflect` to do the real work.
js-zoo-race: Work out the time segment by segment, resolve each animal's promise after that many seconds with `setTimeout`, and let `Promise.race` pick the winner.
